cases.name: Eileen Benson Schnitker
cases.about:
She was a retired nurse. Her niece, Cheryl Benson Kaufman, said her aunt was an extraordinary woman. "The most caring, loving. Always positive, she adored her family. Smart as a damn whip." She worked as a medical assistant from SSM Health until she retired. She loved animals, especially her two dogs.

Schnitker’s son, Jason Schneider, 49, said his mom was a retired medical assistant from SSM Health. She lived with her two dogs. Her son lived a few blocks away. Twice a day, her son would bring his dogs over so they could play with his mom’s dogs; she would make lunch or dinner for her son and they would visit, he said. Schneider was her only child, and he said she was a wonderful mom.
cases.narrative: He allegedly beat her to death with a baseball bat as she sat on the front porch of her Berkely, MO home, and was overheard saying "that felt good" when he stopped swinging the bat. She was violently beaten in the face and head and suffered stab wounds to the abdomen.
